review_note:
REVIEWED AND APPROVED by Joe 2026-07-31 after a full 33-slot walk-through. Two rulings from the review are now BUILT (ORDER 23, 2026-07-31 evening) and this map carries them as data. CHANGED BY ORDER 23, and nothing else in this reviewed map was touched: (1) base_year gained a `drop_when` block — when the lease_type slot resolves to 'Triple Net (please estimate expenses)' the WHOLE table row is deleted from the produced document ('base year row drops most of the time - NNN leases dont include this row'); Full Service and Modified Gross keep it, and an unresolved lease_type keeps it too (`when_unresolved: keep`, because a row is never dropped on a guess). Joe no longer deletes that row by hand. (2) broker_commission gained an `audience` block — `drop_for: [client]` — which drops the row from the CLIENT-COPY artifact only ('we dont like to draw attention to our commission. it only goes out to the listing agent'); the listing-agent working .docx and the record PDF still carry it. Both blocks are read by pipelines/prepare_document.py at finish time, AFTER every fill, so no drop can shift an address out from under a slot.

PROPOSED map, not reviewed. prepare-document refuses this template unless allow_unreviewed:true. Every slot below names the template address it writes and the record field it reads. A slot with kind 'carry' is deliberately NOT written: it is the template's own standing language, left byte-identical and listed in the report as verify-before-sending.

COLOUR CROSS-CHECK (2026-07-31, ORDER 20 fold-in). Joe's convention: blue or red marks text that gets replaced; a letter that goes out is all black. Checked this map against the template's own coloured runs, which are the author's independent list of slots. 100 coloured runs across 34 addresses. COLOURED BUT UNMAPPED (5): table:0:14:0 FF0000 'Exclusivity'; table:0:15:0 FF0000 'Signage'; table:0:16:0 FF0000 'HVAC'; table:0:17:0 FF0000 'Electrical'; table:0:9:0 FF0000 'Base Year'. MAPPED AND MARKED BY A CONTENT CONTROL instead of a colour, correctly mapped (2): para:21, para:3. MAPPED BUT UNMARKED EITHER WAY (2): table:0:10:1, table:0:11:1. NOTHING WAS ADDED TO THIS MAP: the map is reviewed territory, and a slot found by colour is a candidate for the human reading it, not a change made on its behalf.

SENDABLE FORMAT (Joe's doctrine, 2026-07-31, superseding the old blanket 'clients get PDFs, never working files'): this is a LETTER template, so the WORKING .docx is what goes to the listing agent. They edit and revise it, and that revision IS the negotiation; the PDF is the record and preview copy. Because the .docx is outbound it is SCRUBBED before it routes, of comments, tracked changes, comment authors, custom properties and the authorship metadata inherited from CARR's corporate letterhead. Naming a sendable format is not itself an ask to send: it goes out when Joe asks (decision 41906a30).

slot_kinds.record: reads record fields; unresolved -> the slot is written as an explicit OWED marker, never the template's placeholder number
slot_kinds.option: the template ships pipe-separated alternatives; the caller picks via prepare-document's options argument. No default means the caller MUST choose or the slot is owed.
slot_kinds.carry: template language retained untouched; reported for human verification

letter_date.label: Letter date
letter_date.owed_note: FOUND BY THE RENDER, not by reading the XML: this paragraph is a Word content control bound to //StartDate, so python-docx reports it as empty and the first C-112 draft went out dated October 27, 2023. Any map for a CARR letterhead template must cover its date.

re_line.label: RE line
re_line.template_default: RE: Letter of Intent to Lease | Request for Proposal to Lease
choices: RE: Letter of Intent to Lease
RE: Request for Proposal to Lease
re_line.owed_note: LOI (terms our client would accept) vs RFP (asking the landlord to propose). Different documents.

salutation.label: Salutation
choices: Landlord,
Broker,
salutation.owed_note: Addressed to the listing broker in practice; the landlord form exists for direct owners.

intent_sentence.label: Opening sentence
intent_sentence.template_default: Please prepare an offer... | Our client would consider pursuing a lease agreement...
choices: Please prepare an offer for our consideration based upon the following terms:
Our client would consider pursuing a lease agreement based upon the following terms:
intent_sentence.owed_note: Must agree with the RE line: the ask form goes with RFP, the terms form with LOI.

financing_sentence.label: Financing sentence
financing_sentence.template_default: Dr. ___'s financing is already in place through ___.

segments.literal: 's financing is already in place through

financing_sentence.owed_note: Doctor surname comes from the deal's client_contact participant; the lender has NO record field anywhere today (see the report's schema-gap note).

practice_strength.label: Practice-strength paragraph
practice_strength.template_default: She is an established doctor... | He is... | They are...
choices: She is an established doctor with a thriving practice. She is looking to increase her square footage while enhancing her visibility.
He is an established doctor with a thriving practice. He is looking to increase his square footage while enhancing his visibility.
They are established doctors with a thriving practice. They are looking to increase their square footage while enhancing their visibility.
practice_strength.owed_note: No record field carries a person's pronoun and none should be guessed. The caller states it.

buildout_cost_note.label: TI cost sentence ($110 per RSF)
buildout_cost_note.owed_note: Standing template language carrying a market number. No record field holds a per-deal build-out estimate; verify against the deal's own comparison workbook before sending.

vendor_team_sentence.label: Vendor-team paragraph
vendor_team_sentence.template_default: She | He | They will hire a medical specific architect...
choices: She will hire a medical specific architect, contractor, equipment supplier, technology provider, etc.  Each of these vendors is extremely familiar with this process and works on dozens of these projects per year.  The architect will manage the entire process.

He will hire a medical specific architect, contractor, equipment supplier, technology provider, etc.  Each of these vendors is extremely familiar with this process and works on dozens of these projects per year.  The architect will manage the entire process.

They will hire a medical specific architect, contractor, equipment supplier, technology provider, etc.  Each of these vendors is extremely familiar with this process and works on dozens of these projects per year.  The architect will manage the entire process.
vendor_team_sentence.owed_note: Same pronoun choice as practice_strength; kept as its own slot so the two cannot silently disagree.

segments.literal: 's financial statement and tax returns are prepared and will be provided to the landlord of the prevailing property.

financial_statement_sentence.owed_note: Doctor surname, same source as the financing sentence.

tenant.label: Tenant
tenant.template_default: Client DDS | DMD | OD | MD | DO | DPT | DVM | DC
tenant.owed_note: Credential is an option the caller states (DDS/DMD/OD/MD/DO/DPT/DVM/DC). It is OPTIONAL here on purpose: a missing credential must not cost the tenant name.

premises.label: Premises
premises.owed_note: premises/space rows for the subject property. Zero premises rows exist in the system today.

size.label: Size
size.owed_note: Rentable area from the premises/space record.

lease_term.label: Lease Term
lease_term.owed_note: Term from the newest tenant-side negotiation_round.

commencement_date.label: Commencement Date
commencement_date.template_default: 5 months from mutual execution of lease (Design, CD's, Permitting, Build Out, FF&E)
commencement_date.owed_note: lease.commencement_on. Before a lease row exists this is the negotiated date and the template's standing 5-months language may be the right answer instead — a review question, not a fill.

free_rent.label: Free Rent
free_rent.template_default: 3 months free rent and operating expenses upon lease commencement
free_rent.owed_note: Whether operating expenses are abated during free rent is a separate fact; round.opex_note carries it and this slot deliberately does not assert it.

base_rent.label: Base Rent
base_rent.template_default: $20.00 per RSF I Most Competitive Terms
base_rent.owed_note: THE number. Rate plus its basis from the newest tenant-side negotiation_round; a rate without its basis is refused upstream by record-counter, so it can never arrive bare.

lease_type.label: Lease Type
lease_type.template_default: Full Service | Triple Net (please estimate expenses)
choices: Full Service
Triple Net (please estimate expenses)
Modified Gross
lease_type.owed_note: The structure. lease.opex_structure carries it once a lease exists; before that the caller states it.

base_year.label: Base Year
base_year.owed_note: Conditional language ('if Full Service or Modified Gross'). Only relevant when lease_type is not NNN.

drop_when.why: A triple-net lease has no base year, so the row is about nothing rather than unanswered (Joe, 2026-07-31: 'base year row drops most of the time - NNN leases dont include this row'). Full Service and Modified Gross keep the row. The whole table row is deleted, never blanked: a labelled empty row reads as an omission.

renewal_options.label: Renewal Options
renewal_options.template_default: Two five-year options at then market rates

security_deposit.label: Security Deposit
security_deposit.owed_note: 'Equal to one month's gross rent' is a formula, not a figure, and stays true at any rate. A stated dollar deposit belongs in the report, not in this cell.

ti_allowance.label: TI Allowance
ti_allowance.owed_note: negotiation_round.ti_amount + ti_basis. A self-funded build-out is a real answer here and must be stated, not left as the template's $50.

exclusivity.owed_note: 'Exclusive for specialty in the property' is standing ask language.

hvac.owed_note: Standing CARR spec (1 ton per 350 SF).
hvac.note: Most-common placeholder (1 ton per 350 SF), negotiable per deal like every LOI term (taught rule 2026-07-31); per-use guidance now lives in DNA/Reference vertical guides' MEP sections.

electrical.label: Electrical
electrical.note: Most-common placeholder (3-phase, 200 amp), negotiable per deal (taught rule 2026-07-31); 3-phase is often an over-ask for light uses — see DNA/Reference MEP sections.

broker_commission.label: Broker Commission
broker_commission.owed_note: CARR's own commission ask. NEVER record-derived: the deal's commission columns are Salesforce placeholders that no view may treat as data.
broker_commission.note: CARR's own commission ask — most-common placeholder, negotiable per deal. NEVER record-derived: the deal's commission columns are Salesforce placeholders that no view may treat as data.
